bugs_or_flaws: Coverage: Baseline comparison incomplete - only computed for 3 of 19 valid concepts, not all chemistry-in-context claims can be validated against token baselines.

Sanity check needed on n_alive=4096 (pretrained) vs 3473 (random): This suggests ALL latents fired >=20 times in pretrained. While sparse SAEs do have many non-empty columns, this high count warrants verification that the firing threshold isn't too low for ~1M atom activations.

Confounder: tok_j=13 (Carbon) appears across multiple context_chemistry latents with different concepts - need to verify these aren't just capturing common aliphatic carbons rather than true functional group specificity. The script does check within-token AUROC but doesn't explicitly test against Carbon-only baselines.

Confounder: Global AUROCs (~0.5-0.7) are lower as expected, but the gap between within-token (>=0.9) and global could partly reflect token frequency differences rather than true conditional specificity.

rerun_instructions:
1. Compute token-baseline AUROCs for ALL valid concepts (not just 3) to verify within-token features exceed simple atom-type predictions.
2. For top latents, explicitly test activation mean on C-OH vs aliphatic C-C bonds within the same token subset (e.g., tok_j=150/13).
3. Verify firing threshold: check distribution of firing counts across all 4096 latents to confirm >=20 isn't too low.
4. For Carbon tokens, test whether has_O_neighbor vs fg_ether/alcohol can be distinguished (not just presence of O neighbor). This requires concept-level disambiguation tests.
